idiom_name: protocol-typed async client over URLSession, isolated in an actor
implementation_notes: Define a protocol with async throws methods for exactly the operations the presentation layer needs, implement it with a struct or actor over a shared URLSession's async data(for:) API, and map HTTP status, URLError and DecodingError into an application error enum at the boundary while preserving cancellation. That protocol is the delegate seam tests substitute. What replaces the classic structure: there is no separate lookup component (base URL and credentials come from configuration or dependency injection) and no delegate class hierarchy; use an actor only when the delegate owns mutable cached handles or tokens. Keep the hand-written form when you must aggregate endpoints or adapt legacy callback-based APIs.
pitfalls: URLSession instances are expensive and Apple recommends sharing one; per-request sessions waste connection state.
Mapping every URLError into one unavailable error hides cancellation (CancellationError) and offline states - preserve them.
Actor-isolated methods serialize all calls through the actor; if the delegate only reads immutable configuration, mark it nonisolated.
